kpis.context_note: See kpi_15 — data-realistic as-of gives 84.0% (context only, does not replace this figure).
Supplementary context for kpi_01 only — not the pipeline's authoritative churn definition.

insights.headline: Churn looks catastrophic (94%) but is largely a measurement artefact, not a business crisis
insights.narrative: The pipeline's fixed AS_OF_DATE (2026-08-14) sits well past the dataset's actual last event (2025-10-05), so almost every member reads as churned. Re-anchoring to a data-realistic as-of date drops churn to 84.0% (kpi_15) — still high, but the headline 94.0% should never be quoted to leadership without this context.
insights.supporting_evidence: kpi_01 vs kpi_15 (kpi_summary.csv); PR9/PR11 AS_OF_DATE decision.
insights.business_impact: High — wrong framing risks over-reacting (e.g. panic win-back spend) to a partly artefactual stat.
insights.recommended_action: Always report churn with both figures side by side; treat kpi_15 as the operationally meaningful number.

insights.headline: Activation, not renewal, is where the platform loses members
insights.narrative: Only 18.8% of members log any activity within 7 days of joining (PR10 funnel: 81.2% drop-off at this single stage — the largest of any funnel step). No acquisition channel or demographic segment explains it (all Cramér's V < 0.1, PR12).
insights.business_impact: High — the single highest-leverage retention lever found in the dataset.
insights.recommended_action: Prioritise onboarding UX/timing experiments over channel-targeted acquisition spend.

insights.headline: Activation is quietly improving — the funnel is not 'getting worse'
insights.narrative: Monthly cohort activation rate rose from ~14.6% (late 2024) to ~36.6% (Sep 2025) — the most encouraging non-obvious finding in the dataset, and the opposite of what the 81.2% headline drop-off implies in isolation.
insights.business_impact: Medium — reframes the narrative from 'broken funnel' to 'improving, keep investing'.
insights.recommended_action: Investigate what changed operationally in early 2025 and double down on it.

insights.headline: Churn and activation are platform-wide problems, not a branch-operations issue
insights.narrative: 0 of 40 branches are statistical churn-rate outliers, and 0 branches compound a churn anomaly with bottom-quartile activation — ruling out 'a few bad branches' as the root cause.
insights.business_impact: Medium — redirects investigation away from branch staffing/ops toward product/onboarding.
insights.recommended_action: Do not fund a branch-level operational audit as a churn fix; focus centrally on onboarding.

insights.headline: A small, well-defined 'paid once, never engaged' cohort is ready for direct outreach
insights.narrative: 12 currently-active members trigger nearly all composite risk signals — mostly single-event members paying ₹48K–₹102K per logged session. A short, actionable list, not a diffuse population-wide signal.
insights.business_impact: Medium — small volume, but high win-back value per member and low targeting cost.
insights.recommended_action: Direct outreach (call / PT trial offer) to the 12 flagged members within the next billing cycle.
